title: Lesson 3 Quiz: Inflation, Purchasing Power, and Living Standards
description: A short quiz to check what you learned in this lesson. Submitting it completes the lesson's quiz requirement, and your score is recorded separately.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not reviewed or approved by a human (admin); do not give to students.

Comprehensive audit: l3-q2 key no longer the only hedged choice; l3-q5 rewritten to require expected vs. unexpected inflation reasoning (compound average annual rate stated). Lead QA: q5 distractor d made plausible. Lead QA: q5 explanation matches the revised choice d. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A household basket in Country W cost $250 in the base year and costs $265 this year. What is this year's price index (base year = 100)? (Enter a number only.)
Hypothetical example: Country X's inflation rate fell from 6% last year to 3% this year. What happened to the price level this year?

choices.text: The price level fell, because a drop in inflation means prices went down
The price level fell by 3 percent, the size of the drop in the inflation rate
The price level stayed the same, because inflation is now below last year's rate
The price level still rose, but by 3 percent this year instead of 6 percent

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A worker's nominal wage rises 3% this year while the price index rises 5%. By about what percent does the worker's real wage change? Either the exact formula (1 + nominal growth) ÷ (1 + inflation) − 1 or the shortcut (nominal growth − inflation) is accepted. Round to one decimal place and enter a negative number for a decrease. (Enter a number only, in percent.)
Hypothetical example: A bank makes a one-year loan at a fixed 4% interest rate, expecting 2% inflation. Inflation turns out to be 7%. Who gains from this surprise?

choices.text: The borrower gains, because the loan is repaid with dollars that buy less
The bank gains, because higher prices raise the value of what it is repaid
Neither side gains, because the interest rate was fixed in the contract
Both sides gain, because inflation raises everyone's income in dollars

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Inflation in Country X is 3% every year, and people expect it. In Country Y, inflation also has a compound average annual rate of 3% over ten years, but it swings unpredictably between −2% and 8%. Why do economists see Country Y's inflation as more costly, even though the average rate is the same?

choices.text: Country Y has a higher price level at the end of the ten years than Country X
Surprise swings make the real value of fixed-dollar loans and wages uncertain
Years of deflation in Country Y raise the real wages of workers on fixed dollar pay
Because the average rate is the same, the swings cost about as much as steady expected inflation
